patient_information: A 52-year-old man is brought to an urban hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and poorly controlled hypertension.
history_of_present_illness: Describes 4 days of retro-orbital headache, lethargy, myalgia and fevers that had begun to improve over the last 24 hours.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Presented in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, a high-endemicity area for dengue; his last travel outside the city was several years ago.
vitals: GCS 14/15, temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 105/90 mmHg, heart rate 120 bpm, respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute, peripheral oxygen saturation 93% on air.
physical_exam: Drowsy but rousable, weak radial pulse, normal heart sounds, dull percussion note and reduced breath sounds at both lung bases, mild abdominal distension with shifting dullness, tender 3cm liver edge, unremarkable skin, moderate bilateral pleural effusions, ascites, mild hepatomegaly, and a thickened gallbladder wall.
labs_and_diagnostics: Admission labs (see Table 9.1) showed elevated haematocrit, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, elevated C-reactive protein, elevated urea, creatinine, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and lactate; dengue diagnosis confirmed by Reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) and a positive NS1 ELISA.
differential_diagnosis: Dengue infection, rickettsial infections (e.g., scrub typhus), malaria, leptospirosis, and melioidosis.
management_and_clinical_course: Admitted to a high-dependency unit, received Ringer's lactate solution at varying rates (10mL/kg/hr, then 15mL/kg/hr, then 7mL/kg/hr, then 2mL/kg/hr) with repeat clinical assessments and haematocrit checks; patient was discharged 3 days later after complete recovery.
final_diagnosis: Dengue infection with severe disease, vascular leak, and compensated shock.
